latest_census.notes: The 1979 Population Census is the last and only national count, and it was incomplete ('showed Afghanistan to have 16 million inhabitants'). GHDx record (https://ghdx.healthdata.org/record/afghanistan-population-census-1979) lists its topics as including 'ethnicity' and 'religion'; language is not in that list, so language is recorded as unestablished. Minority Rights Group (https://minorityrights.org/country/afghanistan/): 'Afghanistan has not conducted an official census since 1979'; 'After a failed attempt in 2008, another census began in 2013 and was expected to take six years ... this recent census process will not include questions on language or ethnicity, for fear that the results will be too politicized'. WorldPop (https://www.worldpop.org/case_studies/mapping_afg_pop/): 'it has not been possible to conduct a national population and housing census in Afghanistan since 1979'; official statistics 'are largely based on projections from this 1979 baseline'. IHSN catalogue: https://catalog.ihsn.org/index.php/catalog/932/related_materials. Encyclopaedia Iranica 'CENSUS ii. In Afghanistan': https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/census-ii/. The 1979 census was on the province set of that time, not today's 34.

wikipedia.note: The dedicated '"Ethnic groups in Afghanistan" wikipedia by province table' search was not run. Any province-level ethnic percentages on Wikipedia district/province pages can only be estimates (there is no census to source them from), so those pages would at best carry unofficial figures.

tier_reason: There is no count to build from: the last census was the incomplete 1979 enumeration, whose ethnicity/religion tables were not located and which sits on a different province set; every later attempt failed, and the state's own census design since 2013 explicitly excludes language and ethnicity questions. That is a state-level bar on the fields, not merely a search failure, so a not_collected declaration with this evidence is the right output. Religion (99.7% Muslim nationally) has no subnational count either.
recommended_action: Declare ethnicity and language `not_collected` at both levels with the reason 'no census since 1979; the census begun in 2013 excludes language and ethnicity questions (Minority Rights Group; WorldPop)', and religion `not_collected` with 'no census since 1979'. Do not fill from the Commons ethnic map or from Wikipedia province estimates -- neither is a count. Two searches remain worth one attempt each if the budget is restored: whether any SDES provincial report tabulates mother tongue (the only post-1979 sub-provincial enumeration, 13 provinces), and whether the 1979 provincial tables are reproduced anywhere online (historical note only).

summary: Afghanistan has had no census since the incomplete 1979 enumeration, which did ask ethnicity and religion but whose provincial tables were not found online and which used a different province set from today's 34. The census begun in 2013 was designed without language or ethnicity questions because the results would be too politicised, so even a completed count would not carry the fields. The only sub-provincial enumeration since is the UNFPA/NSIA Socio-Demographic and Economic Survey, run in 13 of 34 provinces down to district and village, whose listed topics do not include ethnicity, religion or language (not confirmed either way -- the specific search did not run). HDX holds boundaries, population estimates and DHS health indicators for Afghanistan, not ethnic composition; a district ethnic map on Wikimedia Commons is a drawing, not a table. Tier C: declare all three fields not_collected at both levels with the Minority Rights Group and WorldPop evidence. The Wikipedia checks were not run because the session's search budget ran out.
